record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: For every real gamma with |gamma| < 2, is every integer sequence {a_n}_n satisfying 0 <= a_n + gamma a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} < 1 eventually periodic?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Let |γ| < 2. Prove that each integer sequence {an}n satisfying 0 ≤ an + γan+1 + an+2 < 1 is eventually periodic.
This ‘Salem type periodicity’ problem is related to the orbit of piecewise isometry

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be a real number with $|\gamma|<2$. Prove or disprove: every sequence $\{a_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ of integers satisfying
$$0 \le a_n + \gamma\, a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} < 1 \quad \text{for all } n\ge 0$$
is eventually periodic (i.e., there exist integers $N\ge 0$ and $p\ge 1$ such that $a_{n+p}=a_n$ for all $n\ge N$).
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem (sometimes called the Salem-type periodicity problem), connected to piecewise isometries and beta-expansions. Web search did not surface a resolution; it continues to be cited as an open question in surveys of beta-expansion problems.

status_evidence.title: Periodic expansion of one by Salem numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodicity related to Salem numbers; the general Salem-type periodicity question remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Related Salem periodicity questions are still active research topics.
